bullets.title: September NFP misses hard (-29k vs 90k est), reducing October hike odds to ~16-22%
bullets.body: September nonfarm payrolls came in at +29k vs consensus +90k, with prior months revised down net -60k. Unemployment rose to 4.2% (driven by rising labor force participation, not layoffs), and average hourly earnings grew just +0.1% m/m (+3.0% y/y)—well below the Fed's 3.5-4.0% implicit target. Multiple desks read this as pushing the next hike to December at earliest, with market pricing compressing to only 22-25 bps of additional tightening through year-end.

bullets.title: Accenture +17% on F4Q beat; bookings inflect, FY27 guidance beats—broad software sympathy
bullets.body: ACN reported F4Q revenue of $18.68B (+7% cc, top of guidance), EPS $3.29 vs $3.18 est, and bookings of $22.2B (+5% cc), reversing a prior quarter decline. FY27 guidance of +3-6% cc revenue growth beat consensus. The print lifted IT services and software broadly (TEAM +3%, HUBS +3%, NOW +3%, CRM +2%), interpreted as confirmation that enterprise AI spending is converting into durable revenue.

bullets.title: Micron crushes F4Q, guides F1Q well above Street; memory supply tight through CY28
bullets.body: MU reported F4Q revenue of $54.23B (+5.7% above consensus) and guided F1Q to $61.5B (+7.1% above), with gross margin at 86.25% (the stated floor for FY27). Management confirmed >75% of CY27 output already committed via 26 long-term agreements, HBM4 pricing up 100-150% YoY in CY27, and plans to return 100% of excess cash via buybacks starting December 9. Supply-demand imbalance expected to worsen in CY27-28 vs. CY26.

bullets.title: Morgan Stanley reinstates NVDA as Top Pick ($300 PT, 30% upside) post-NDR on Feynman roadmap and agentic AI
bullets.body: MS's Joe Moore reinstated NVDA at Overweight with a $300 PT (~20x CY27 EPS) after management meetings highlighted a customer base ~50% outside hyperscalers (neoclouds, sovereigns, enterprise), the Vera Rubin ramp, and the Feynman architecture targeting $60B+ revenue per GW by 2028 (25x Blackwell tokens). NVDA also announced a $150B buyback increase (total $235B through FY28), the largest in history. Agentic AI inference workloads seen as driving 10x incremental tokens vs. human usage.

bullets.title: Eurozone CPI surged to 3.8% YoY in September; ECB December hike now base case, France spreads at crisis levels
bullets.body: Euro area headline HICP jumped to 3.76% YoY (from 3.2%), driven by energy at +18.8% YoY and sticky services at +3.2%. JPMorgan and multiple banks now see a December ECB 25bp hike as near-certain, with October a skip. Separately, French OAT-Bund spreads widened to 127-152bp—levels not seen since 2011-12—on fiscal credibility concerns (debt at 118% GDP, deficit target of 5% for 2027 viewed as unachievable). Moody's sovereign review for France is scheduled for October 23.

bullets.title: US 10-year yield hit 5.29-5.34%—highest since 2002—as growth and inflation reaccelerate
bullets.body: Treasury yields surged 53bp in September to 5.29%, with the 10-year posting its largest quarterly jump since 1994. Drivers include an upward GDP revision to 2.2% (Q2), sticky core PCE at 3.0% YoY, ISM Manufacturing Prices Paid at 77.9 (6.8pp jump on tariffs/steel/energy), and elevated energy prices. JPM forecasts the 10-year at 5.20% near-term, declining to 5.05% by year-end. Corporate bond spreads widened to their widest since March and 30-year mortgage rates hit 7.30%.

bullets.title: Oil touched $108 Brent on Hormuz tensions; energy reduced to minimum as WTI breaks $92 support
bullets.body: Brent crude surged above $100-$108 during the week on Iran-Strait of Hormuz supply risk, Ukraine strikes on Russian refineries, and tight diesel markets. However, by Friday WTI broke the $92 support level and fell ~4.8% to ~$88, signaling lower highs. Barclays raised its Q4 Brent forecast to $115. Hedgeye, Citadel, and multiple sell-side desks reduced energy exposure to minimums on the WTI signal, rotating into technology and growth assets.

bullets.title: Fed speakers (Jefferson, Williams, Kashkari) lean against October hike; market pricing 4-5 hikes vs. Fed's 2-3
bullets.body: Multiple Fed officials signaled a high bar for October action: Vice Chair Jefferson said more time is needed, NY Fed's Williams flagged no urgency, and Dallas Fed's Logan was the sole hawk backing 50bp more. Markets were pricing 4-5 total hikes vs. the FOMC's own 2-3 signal, creating a potential relief rally in rates if data remains soft. The gap widened further after the weak payroll print pushed October hike odds to 16-22%.

bullets.title: Hedgeye Q4 macro: Quad 2 (growth + inflation accelerating); long XLK, META, MSFT, NVDA; short XLY, XLF
bullets.body: Hedgeye's macro framework places the US in Quad 2 (growth and inflation both accelerating) through at least January 2027, supported by easy comps, tax stimulus, AI capex returns, and tight labor. Core longs are XLK (hit ATH), META, MSFT, NVDA, MU, AAPL; explicit shorts include XLY (-6.7% Q3), XLF (-7.5% Q3), XLU, XLI. Oil trimmed to minimum after WTI's first lower-high fractal signal. VIX contained below 17-19 ('investable bucket').

bullets.title: AVGO assembles $42-60B financing for Anthropic AI infrastructure; AMD acquires World Labs for $8.2B
bullets.body: Broadcom agreed to lend Anthropic up to $42B for chip infrastructure purchases (convertible to equity), part of a broader $60B financing package. Separately, AMD announced an $8.2B all-stock acquisition of Fei-Fei Li's World Labs (spatial/3D AI for robotics and physical AI), with Li becoming AMD EVP and chief scientist. Amazon also disclosed plans to offload ~$8B of Nvidia chips via an SPV to lighten its balance sheet.

bullets.title: META launches Enterprise Platform; hires MongoDB CEO—MDB falls 18-26% on leadership shock
bullets.body: Meta launched Meta Enterprise Platform (Muse agent, Business Agent, Muse API, Muse Code) aimed at enterprise customers, and poached MongoDB CEO CJ Desai as Chief Enterprise Platform Officer. MongoDB's stock fell 18-26% as Desai had joined less than a year prior and was central to its go-to-market for Atlas AI. Dev Ittycheria returned as interim CEO; MDB reaffirmed FY27 guidance. Meta Muse separately hit 3M weekly users and 5M downloads within 22 days of launch, faster than ChatGPT, Grok, or Claude.

bullets.title: FCC optical transceiver restrictions on China likely at 3.2T generation; LITE, COHR rally 7-11%
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley and JPM reported that DC meetings indicate FCC rules restricting Chinese-built optical transceivers are likely, phased in starting at the 3.2T generation (2028+ ramp). A 65% US-content BOM workaround allows module vendors to remain viable. LITE surged +7.7% and COHR +10.9% on the news, with analysts citing laser margin upside (50%+) as the primary read-through vs. lower-margin transceiver assembly.

bullets.title: US 2026 midterms: prediction markets now price >60% Democratic Senate flip; regime-change risk rising
bullets.body: Goldman, Jefferies, and JPMorgan all flagged that prediction markets price >60% Democratic Senate majority and >90% Democratic House majority, far above investor positioning (only 9% expected a sweep in August). Key Senate races include NC, ME, OH, AK, TX. Jefferies and JPMorgan both note September-October historically underperform in midterm years, with Q4 post-election historically +9.5%. A Democratic sweep would reprice healthcare (Medicaid cuts reversed), tech (antitrust oversight), and renewable energy (spending support).

bullets.title: AI data center buildout faces acute power and regulatory bottlenecks; supportive states shrinking from 27 to ~15
bullets.body: Multiple research teams (22V, JPM, Jefferies) flagged that US AI data center demand of 107GW through 2030 exceeds confirmed supply by 37GW, while post-midterm state-level regulatory actions may reduce AI-friendly states from 27 to ~15. Texas (35-47% of announced capacity) faces TCEQ permit delays and ERCOT queue reviews through December. Over 800 local moratoria enacted since June 2025. Companies with already-permitted power sites (CRWV, RIOT) have strategic optionality.

bullets.title: Toshiba HDD capacity expansion headline spooked STX/WDC (down 11%/8%), but bulls say buy the dip
bullets.body: Toshiba announced a ¥60B (~$380M) expansion of Philippines HDD factory to double capacity by FY27, targeting 30% market share from 10% currently. STX fell 11% and WDC fell 7-8% on the news. However, Citi and MS both maintained Buy ratings with $1,300/$740 PTs, noting Toshiba relies on external media/heads suppliers, lags on max-capacity drives (30-34TB vs competitors), and faces 12+ month hyperscaler qualification cycles. Supply-demand gap of >300 EB remains; capacity sold through CY28.

bullets.title: Anthropic IPO filing reveals $42B net loss, $518B cloud commitments; $2T valuation target requires 40x revenue growth
bullets.body: Anthropic's S-1 shows FY25 revenue of $4.6B (12x YoY), operating loss of $8B, and net loss of $42B (mostly financing charges). The company plans to spend $518B on cloud/compute obligations over 10+ years (~$111B with Google, $110B with Amazon, $31B with Microsoft). Two customers represent 25% of revenue. The IPO targets a $2T valuation implying ~$190-200B in 2028 revenue—a 40x+ expansion. OpenAI also reached ~$70B ARR, up from $40B in August.

bullets.title: Google Gemini 4 Argon launch removes key AI overhang; GOOGL buy at $420-447 PT
bullets.body: Google released Gemini 4 Argon, ranking top across 14 of 19 benchmarks vs. GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1, with a 1M-token output limit and introductory pricing 75-80% below Claude at $2-4/1M tokens. Citi (Buy, $447 PT) and JPMorgan (OW, $420 PT) both called it a key overhang removal and restart of Google's product cycle. Internal employee skepticism on real-world coding performance remains a watch item. TPU monetization (projected $30B+ in 2027) was also reaffirmed.

bullets.title: FHFA moves to bi-merge credit reports and VantageScore parity, threatening EFX/TRU/FICO EPS 7-8%
bullets.body: FHFA Director Pulte directed Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac to shift from tri-merge (three bureaus) to bi-merge (two) and adopt a single pricing grid treating VantageScore and FICO equally. This could be ~5-7% dilutive to EFX and TRU EPS and represents a structural shift in FICO's mortgage pricing power. Rocket Mortgage designated VantageScore 4.0 as its preferred model. UBS maintained Buy on EFX ($220 PT) citing proprietary data, while JPM flagged large-cap bank NII tailwinds from higher rates.

bullets.title: Brazil election first round Oct 4; closest race ever with market implications for BRL, local bonds, and equities
bullets.body: Brazil's presidential first round is October 4, described by JPMorgan as the closest ever, with Lula in a narrow first-round lead and runoff polls showing a virtual tie with Senator Flávio Bolsonaro. BofA recommends short EUR/BRL ahead of the election (cheap, high carry, potential market-positive outcome), long NTN-F 2037 bonds, and notes foreign investors are lightly positioned. GS and JPM are hosting webinars; prediction markets imply >60% chance of Bolsonaro winning runoff.

bullets.title: 22V and JPM shift tactically bullish into earnings; AI broadening thesis from infra to software adopters
bullets.body: JPMorgan formally moved to Tactically Bullish, citing stabilizing yields, stronger-than-expected growth PMIs (flash PMI at 58.4), and Q3 EPS tracking +28.9% with 15% margins (second-best ever). 22V's regime model shows 70% probability of remaining in Normal Expansion over six months, with recession probability at only 10%. Both houses recommend staying long Price/EPS Momentum factors into earnings and favor AI adopters/enablers (NVDA, MSFT, META, ACN) over broad market.
